blogPosts.title: How Much Does an Office Fitout Cost in Southbank in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Wondering about office fitout costs in Southbank? We break down pricing per square metre, key factors, and how to budget for your Melbourne commercial space.
body: Planning an office fitout in Southbank? The cost can vary widely depending on the size of your space, the level of fitout, and the materials you choose. In 2026, typical office fitout costs in Melbourne range from $800 to $2,500 per square metre, with Southbank prices sitting at the higher end due to premium locations and building requirements.

A basic fitout — think new carpet, paint, and standard workstations — might start around $800 per square metre. A mid-range fitout with better lighting, breakout areas, and quality joinery can cost $1,200 to $1,800 per square metre. High-end fitouts with custom furniture, advanced AV systems, and architectural features can exceed $2,500 per square metre.

Your location in Southbank also affects costs. Many commercial buildings in the area have specific requirements for fire safety, accessibility, and heritage compliance, which can add to the budget. It's important to factor in these local regulations early in the planning process to avoid surprises.

Another key cost driver is the condition of your existing space. If you're moving into a shell, you'll need to budget for base building works like HVAC, electrical, and plumbing. If you're refurbishing an existing fitout, you might save on structural costs but still need to update finishes and technology.

At RPC Group, we provide detailed, fixed-price quotes after an on-site consultation. We'll walk you through every line item, from demolition to handover, so you know exactly what you're paying for. No hidden fees, no surprises.

blogPosts.title: Retail Fitout Design Trends in Melbourne for 2026
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover the top retail fitout trends in Melbourne for 2026, from sustainable materials to immersive brand experiences. RPC Group shares expert insights for Southbank retailers.
body: Retail fitouts in Melbourne are evolving fast, and 2026 is all about creating immersive, sustainable, and flexible spaces. Southbank retailers are leading the charge, with fitouts that blend digital and physical experiences to engage customers and drive sales.

One of the biggest trends is the use of sustainable materials. From recycled timber to low-VOC paints, eco-friendly fitouts are becoming the norm. Customers are increasingly drawn to brands that prioritise sustainability, and a green fitout can be a powerful marketing tool.

Another trend is flexible layouts that can adapt to changing seasons or product lines. Movable walls, modular shelving, and multi-purpose zones allow retailers to refresh their space without a full renovation. This is especially popular in Southbank's high-traffic retail precincts.

Lighting is also a key focus. In 2026, retailers are using dynamic lighting systems that change colour and intensity to create different moods throughout the day. This not only enhances the shopping experience but also highlights products effectively.

Technology integration is another must-have. From digital signage to interactive displays, tech-enabled fitouts help retailers tell their brand story and capture customer data. Southbank's tech-savvy shoppers expect a seamless omnichannel experience.

At RPC Group, we specialise in retail fitouts that combine style with function. Whether you're opening a new store in Southbank or refreshing an existing one, we can help you design a space that stands out. Contact us for a free consultation.

blogPosts.title: Office Make Good in Melbourne: A Complete Guide for Tenants
blogPosts.excerpt: Learn everything about office make good in Melbourne, from lease obligations to cost-saving tips. RPC Group explains the process for Southbank tenants.
body: If you're a commercial tenant in Southbank, you've probably heard of 'make good' — the obligation to restore your leased space to its original condition before vacating. It's a common clause in Melbourne commercial leases, and getting it wrong can cost you thousands.

The make good process typically involves removing all fitouts, repairing walls and floors, and reinstating services like electrical and HVAC. In Southbank, many buildings also require you to comply with specific fire safety and accessibility standards during the restoration.

One of the biggest mistakes tenants make is leaving the make good to the last minute. A thorough make good can take several weeks, especially if your fitout is complex. Starting early gives you time to plan, budget, and avoid penalties from your landlord.

Costs for office make good in Melbourne vary widely. A simple office with standard finishes might cost $50 to $100 per square metre, while a high-end fitout with custom joinery and AV systems can cost $200 per square metre or more. Getting a professional assessment early helps you budget accurately.

At RPC Group, we've handled hundreds of make good projects across Southbank and Melbourne. We manage the entire process, from stripping out fitouts to final inspection, ensuring you meet your lease obligations and get your bond back.

blogPosts.title: Restaurant Fitout Costs in Melbourne: What to Expect in 2026
blogPosts.excerpt: Planning a restaurant fitout in Melbourne? We break down the costs, from kitchen compliance to dining room design, with tips for Southbank hospitality venues.
body: Opening a restaurant in Southbank? The fitout is one of the biggest expenses, and costs can vary dramatically depending on the size, style, and complexity of your venue. In 2026, restaurant fitout costs in Melbourne typically range from $2,000 to $5,000 per square metre.

The kitchen is often the most expensive part of a restaurant fitout. Commercial kitchens require specialised equipment, ventilation, fire suppression systems, and compliance with health regulations. A basic kitchen fitout can cost $100,000, while a high-end setup can exceed $300,000.

Dining room design is another major cost factor. From flooring and lighting to furniture and decor, every element contributes to the ambience. In Southbank, where competition is fierce, a standout fitout can be the difference between a full house and an empty room.

Don't forget about compliance. Melbourne restaurants must meet strict standards for fire safety, accessibility, and food handling. These requirements can add 10-20% to your fitout budget, so it's important to factor them in from the start.
